Irene —

We can provide logs (attached a small KPI dump) and traces — ops team are on rotations. We need an immediate routing change: can you either divert traffic to US-WEST-3 or initiate a controlled drain of affected AZs so we can regain baseline performance? Sapphire is flagging this as P1 and asks for exec visibility.

Attachments: sapphire_kpi_dump.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Diane

Folks — looping in SRE + routing. Diane, thanks for the quick heads-up and the KPI snapshot. We're treating this as customer P1 and will propose an immediate mitigation plan. Key constraints: we must avoid large cache churn and avoid invalidating long-lived KV cache entries that Sapphire relies on.

Proposed immediate action (need confirmation):
- Start a controlled "gray-route" that shifts 15% of Sapphire's traffic to US-WEST-3 within 10m for fast validation.
- If error/latency improves, increase to 50% in 20m, then full diversion if stable.
- Simultaneously start a phased AZ drain on the most impacted AZ (az-2) to force routing decisions without full cross-region failover.

Ben/Hannah: can you confirm whether the gray-route will preserve KV prefixes and whether we should enable prefix caching bypass? Also, please advise timeline and the rollback play. I attached a quick draft playbook.

Irene Choi
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 17 May 2028 08:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: URGENT - US-WEST2 latency spike causing 5xxs and throughput drop

Irene — quick technical note and plan. I've looked at the KPI dump; az-2 within us-west-2 shows elevated kernel queueing and ~30% increase in token processing times, which suggests local saturation on the inference nodes rather than upstream network.

Plan (immediate):
1) Launch gray-route (15%) to us-west-3 using routing policy set "phased-validation-v2". This preserves user routing keys and should keep KV cache prefixes intact for the shifted requests. Expect slightly higher cold-start latency for first-minute requests.
2) Initiate phased drain of us-west-2 az-2: cordon new sessions, allow in-flight KV windows to close (~90s typical), and then stop accepting new inference sessions from that AZ — target 30m to fully drain.
3) Monitor: token latency, 5xx, and tail P99 every 60s. Alert to pager if P95 > 1.2s or 5xx > 1%.
4) If gray-route shows improvement (>50% reduction in 5xx and >20% latency reduction within 15m), increase shift to 65% and continue drain; otherwise, rollback to previous routing in 5m.

Risks: cache warm-up in us-west-3 could temporarily spike token time for heavy endpoints; we should throttle batch sizes for shifted traffic for first 10m.

Attachments: proposed_gray_route_playbook_v1.pdf (pdf)

Ben Carter
Principal SRE — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
